author: edda
text: Interim text (sc-572): the runner retracts streamed text at the round's first new tool call (and at the tool result for text written after a call) with a new record {type:'interim', text:<status line>}; it means 'all answer text so far was progress'. ws.py clears its tokens, the browser clears its stream text and shows the line as status, so stored = live by construction. Chosen over buffering (kills streaming of the real answer) and segment offsets (two indexes to keep in sync). Cost: interim text is visible as answer for the moment between its first token and the tool call.

author: edda
text: A turn superseded or dropped while text streams saves exactly what the live view held (the not-yet-retracted segment) as status=partial, never indexed (partials never reach the KB). Text already retracted as interim is gone from ws.py's tokens and is never saved. Reason: we can't know mid-segment whether it is interim, and the drop path in the browser keeps the same text, so reload equals live.

author: edda

author: edda
text: Status line: first sentence of the latest thought paragraph of the current model call (thought partials accumulated per call, the non-partial aggregate used only when no partials came), heading lines count as sentences, cleaned server-side (ANSI, Cc/Cf incl. bidi, markdown markers, whitespace) and capped at 80 chars; at most 1 event/s; none from authors other than the root agent; none once the segment has answer text. Browser caps again (120) and renders text only. Generic 'Thinking… Ns' after 3 s without any turn event while no tool is casting and no thought line is current (thought line cleared on tool_end).

author: edda
text: Retraction guard (080 review SEC-001): an interim retraction happens only for text <= 600 chars (INTERIM_MAX_CHARS) in a round with no presenting call (create_chart, propose_profile_changes = PRESENTING_TOOLS), and never after any text was kept as answer (then later text joins with a paragraph, sc-302 style). A turn ending with no answer after a retraction re-emits the last retracted text as a token ahead of the no-answer message (pre-080 behaviour for that edge, so nothing is lost; never indexed since the turn is empty). Residual: a short (<600) answer followed by a gathering call and then a non-empty closing line is still retracted; length can't tell a 250-char troubleshooting note from a 250-char answer, and restoring on short finals would bring back exactly the sc-572 paragraphs. SEC-002: ws.py sends the interim frame before clearing tokens, so a drop noticed at that send saves the browser's text as the partial; residual: a frame accepted by the kernel but lost in transit still leaves the text local-only (not stored, not in the PDF, gone on reopen).
